h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: When edge 5 already delivers conv3x3 features into node 3, a parallel conv3x3 from node 1 is partly redundant, so its marginal gain shrinks.
An identity 0->3 shortcut turns the deep 0->1->2->3 conv path into an easily optimised residual branch, so adding conv depth on edge 2 pays off more.
A conv3x3 on edge 2 gives node 2 a strong learned input, so degrading edge 1 to pooling costs less than when node 2 depends on edge 1.
When edge 0 is conv3x3, node 2 still gets learned features via node 1 and edge 2, so deleting the direct 0->2 edge loses less.
Without a direct 0->3 path, a conv1x1 from node 1 supplies a short, low-depth route to the output that is otherwise missing.
A skip on edge 2 cheaply relays edge 0's conv features into node 2, which is worth more when those upstream features are learned rather than trivial.
When node 3 relies on a deep conv path via edge 5, removing the direct input route removes an easy gradient path and hurts more.
An identity 0->3 edge pairs with the conv on edge 4 to form a residual block, mirroring the top-ranked NAS-Bench-201 cells.
With edge 1 already conv3x3, node 2 has a strong learned input, so a second conv route into node 2 adds less.
With edge 0 pooled, a skip on edge 4 injects blurred, unprocessed features straight into the output sum, diluting it.
